A cross-platform launcher normally spawns child processes with the shell disabled. For one case it enables the shell: on Windows, when the resolved executable ends in .cmd or .bat. The comment states that Node cannot execute Windows batch shims with the shell disabled, and that the package managers it must launch are exactly such shims.

The arguments passed in that branch are a fixed list of flags chosen by the calling code, and each is quoted before being joined. No caller-supplied or file-supplied text reaches the argument list.

Decide whether enabling the shell in this branch is an injection defect.
